newsitem.title: INDIA: India INDAL starts output in new plants.
newsitem.headline: India INDAL starts output in new plants.

text.p: The Indian Aluminium Company Ltd (INDAL) said it had started production in some of its expansion and upgrading projects.
In a statement on Monday, INDAL listed the projects and works as follows --
--Doubling of special alumina facilities at Belgaum in the southern state of Karnataka.
--An additional 50 kilotonnes per annum capacity of metallurgical grade alumina.
--A state-of-the-art twin head poly extruder at its foil plant at Kalwa to provide higher value addition to foil laminates.
--A 25 kilotonne per annum recycling plant at Taloja in the western state of Maharashtra, which is expected to add 16 kilotonnes to INDAL's metal supplies in 1997/98 (April-March).
"The company is taking measures to bring down inventories and costs," INDAL's vice-chairman and managing director, Tapan Mitra, said in the statement.
"The international aluminium and alumina prices are now showing signs of recovery, which, if sustained, should improve performance in the coming months."
Mitra said demand growth was slower than expected, particularly in key domestic market segments like capital goods, consumer durables and refractories.
"Growth in foil and packaging industry was less than half of last year. Sheet demand too, belying forecasts, did not pick up over last three months," the statement said.
"This is partly attributable to de-stocking in the industry, as well as the generally depressed state of the economy which is affecting all aluminium consuming industries," it added.

"Larger-than-envisaged imports of semi-fabricated products as well as the demand recession in key domestic segments led to sharp price cuts by domestic and foreign competition, putting sales realisations under greater pressure.
"Cost of money continued to remain high for most aluminium customers and this forced manufacturers to provide extended credit," the statement added.
